reason: This text describes King Josiah's reign and his religious reforms, emphasizing qualities such as doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord, following God's law, making covenants with God, and implementing extensive religious reforms. While the text mentions destruction of idolatrous items and killing of idolatrous priests as part of religious purification (וַיִּזְבַּח אֶת־ כָּל־ כֹּהֲנֵי הַבָּמוֹת - 'he slaughtered all the priests of the high places'), this violence is directed at religious opposition and false worship practices, not against 'unruly people' as a general leadership discipline. The text presents the model for Josiah's good leadership as obedience to Torah, religious righteousness, and covenant-keeping with God, not as violence toward subjects who are disobedient or unruly.
